### Observed differences

- A09 occurrences per trace rose from about 1.9 to 4.3, and the share of traces with more than one occurrence rose from 39% to 60%. [OCC002]
- A03 and A14 occurrences per trace fell from about 1.1 to 0.5, and their recurrence support dropped from 27.5% to 0% (no trace has them more than once). [OCC001, OCC003]
- A11 participation rose from 27.5% to 47% of traces, and its median relative position moved from 0.40 to 0.11. [POS002]
- A03 and A14 also moved earlier (median from ~0.36 to ~0.17 and ~0.32 to ~0.20). [POS001, POS003]
- Outgoing from A15: before about 38% to A01 and 41% to A09; after 95% to A09 and 0% to A01. [DIR006]
- Outgoing from A13: before about 36% to A15 and 35% to A09; after 71% to A09 and 8% to A15. [DIR004]
- Outgoing from A06: before 86% to A01 and 7% to A14; after 99% to A01 and 0% to A14. [DIR002]
- Outgoing from A01: before 8.7% to A15; after 0% to A15, with A13 and A09 shares increasing. [DIR001]
- Outgoing from A14: before 18% to A11 and 10% to A12; after 4% to A11 and 34% to A12. [DIR005]
- A03 and A11: before they co-occurred in 27.5% of traces and always interleaved/repeated; after they co-occur in 47% and are ordered (A11 before A03 in 33%, A03 before A11 in 14%). [REL001]
- A11 and A14: before A14 occurred alone in 23% of traces and they interleaved in 27.5%; after they co-occur in 47% with A11 before A14 in 38.5%. [REL004]
- A03 and A14: interleaving disappeared (27.5% to 0%), replaced by ordered occurrences. [REL002]
- A09 and A13: interleaving increased from 39% to 59.5%. [REL003]
- LAG: A01 to A11 gap decreased (lag 1–2 increased), A14 to A03 gap decreased (lag 1 from 15% to 68%), A15 to A01 gap increased (lag 1 from 8% to 0%), A09 to A01 gap increased (lag 2 decreased, lag 4 increased). [LAG003, LAG010, LAG011, LAG006]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a change in the routing around A15, A13 and A09: in the later window, A15 and A13 both lead predominantly to A09 (instead of A15 leading to A01 and A13 leading to A15), and A09 is executed more often and repeated more. This is directly shown by the successor shifts in DIR006, DIR004, DIR001 and DIR002, and by the increased occurrence and recurrence of A09 in OCC002. The increased interleaving between A09 and A13 (REL003) and the lag changes (e.g., A15–A01 gap widening, A09–A01 gap widening) are consistent with this re‑routing.

Other differences: A03 and A14 become less frequent and no longer repeat, and A11 appears earlier and co‑occurs with A03 and A14 in an ordered way (A11 before them). A14’s successor shifts from A11 to A12. These changes are not part of the main routing hypothesis but are clearly present.

A competing explanation that cannot be fully ruled out is that the observed differences reflect a rare variant that became dominant in the later sample; however, the large number of qualifying items (29 vs. 0.43 expected by chance) and the consistency across multiple indicators make this unlikely.
